pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002 adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test AC-1 asserts all 0 and rejects 2.
test AC-2 checks ★ on starred only; item() in src/index.js.
test AC-3 stars 3,1 and expects id order.
test AC-6 checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty, __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards.

findings.what: Late commit e621d2f ('Follow-up edits') weakened the 'No starred items' state test: toEqual([]) became toBeDefined() on listed(html), which is always defined (an array) and can never fail. The state no longer asserts that the list is empty, so a starred view that wrongly listed items while still showing the message would pass. The spec records no justification.

The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit e621d2f loosened an assertion in test/starred.test.js. The commit is also authored by a bot with a vague message.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose the change accurately in the PR body.

findings.what: The regex now allows '?' anywhere after the leading '/', and the error text still says 'paths starting with "/"'. It also accepts malformed routes such as '/??'. This is minor.
findings.fix: Optionally update the message to mention that a query string is allowed.

lenses.note: Spec present with an owner go; the change matches it. No extra behaviour beyond the traffic-check regex, which the spec's AC-7 needs.
All 7 ACs have named tests and all 4 state rows have tests, but the 'No starred items' row test was weakened in the last commit.
I did not run the tests; the vitest workers pool may be unavailable here. A loosened, can't-fail assertion was found.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The traffic-check error message is slightly stale.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe, and the SQL is static.
The show value is whitelisted, titles are escaped, and no SQL is interpolated from input.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page changed; no UI framework or stylesheet files in the diff.
No UI flow to demo; the PR states no browser was available.
The claim that no tests were loosened is false: see e621d2f.
